title: 3 dead, 3 injured after domestic violence shooting in Spokane County, WA
text:
3 dead, 3 injured after domestic violence shooting in Spokane County, WA
SPANGLE, Wash. - Three people died and two Spokane County Sheriff's deputies were critically injured Tuesday after a domestic violence call escalated into a deadly shooting in a rural area south of Spokane.
3 dead, 2 deputies critically injured in Spangle, WA shooting
What we know:
Authorities said a woman fled to a neighbor's house for help Tuesday afternoon after being shot by her brother in Spangle.
Timeline:
Deputies responded to the scene at 2:25 p.m. and moved in to contain the property. When they attempted to enter the home at 3:15 p.m. to rescue others inside, they were met with gunfire. Two deputies were shot and suffered life-threatening injuries.
Spokane County Sheriff John Nowels confirmed the suspect is dead. Another person was found dead outside the home, bringing the total death toll to three. Three other victims were transported to Sacred Heart Medical Center.
What we don't know:
Authorities have not released the names of the deputies, the suspect, or the victims, nor have they provided an update on the current medical conditions of those hospitalized.
This is a developing story. Check back for updates.
The Source: Information in this story came from the Spokane County Sheriff's Office, Washington State Patrol and original reporting by FOX 13 Seattle.

title: Man charged with murder, admitted to shooting woman in Harris County trailer home
text:
Man charged with murder, admitted to shooting woman in Harris County trailer home
HOUSTON - A dispute turned deadly in northwest Harris County after a woman was shot and killed inside a trailer home, according to Harris County Sheriff's Office.
Deadly shooting in northwest Harris County
What we know:
Sergeant Jason Brown reported deputies were called to a home on Proctor Street near the intersection of State Highway 249 and Antoine Drive after a neighbor said they heard gunshots and saw a man leaving a trailer home.
When deputies arrived, they found 35-year-old Blanca Alvarez dead inside the trailer with gunshot wounds.
Investigators searched the surrounding area and located the suspect, 50-year-old Wilson Salamanca. He was taken into custody without incident.
Sgt. Brown said Alvarez and Salamanca lived together at the location but were not married. Salamanca admitted to detectives he shot Alvarez during a domestic altercation.
Salamanca was officially charged with murder and booked into the Harris County Jail.
What we don't know:
The relationship between Alvarez and Salamanca is unknown.
The Source: Information in this article was provided by the Harris County Sheriff's Office.
label_rationale: Vụ bạo lực gia đình, tin đã có kết luận bắt giữ; tông buồn là chính. Mức chắc chắn: cao.

title: Man arrested after unattended Miami patrol car stolen with officer's rifle, vest inside
text:
Man arrested after unattended Miami patrol car stolen with officer's rifle, vest inside
A man was arrested Tuesday afternoon after police said he stole an unattended City of Miami-marked patrol car outside a convenience store and drove it home with an officer's rifle and bulletproof vest still inside.
Rodne Joseph, 36, faces multiple felony charges, including grand theft of a vehicle, grand theft of a firearm, armed burglary of an unoccupied conveyance, and depriving an officer of means of protection or communication, according to his arrest report.
According to the report, the theft happened around 1:20 p.m. Tuesday near the intersection of Northeast Second Avenue and Northeast 55th Terrace.
A City of Miami police sergeant parked his marked patrol cruiser outside the store and went inside. When he came back a few minutes later, he discovered the vehicle was missing.
The sergeant canvassed the immediate area and broadcast a radio alert notifying surrounding units that his vehicle had just been stolen. Within minutes, the report said the department's Real Time Crime Center tracked the stolen cruiser traveling north along Northeast Second Avenue and Northeast 77th Street.
By 2:14 p.m., a "be on the lookout" alert was issued by multiple law enforcement agencies, describing a suspect wearing a dark shirt and light blue jeans.
How the suspect was detained
At around 3 p.m., a North Miami police officer spotted the marked cruiser parked and unoccupied in front of a home at Northeast 137th Street and 5th Avenue, roughly around five miles from where it was taken, the report states. Auto-theft detectives from the City of Miami Police Department responded to secure the scene.
The report noted that convenience store surveillance video, reviewed by investigators, showed a man matching the broadcast description walking southbound along Northeast Second Avenue toward the cruiser's driver's door before the car was seen pulling away and heading northbound.

title: 16-year-old girl struck with shrapnel 'square in the mouth' after partygoer tosses shock absorber into bonfire, causing explosion: Family
text:
Cops in Arizona are searching for the person who allegedly chucked a car part into a bonfire, causing an explosion that seriously hurt a 16-year-old girl.
Phoenix police said the incident happened around 10:30 p.m. on Oct. 30 in the middle of the desert near New River and Saddle Mountain roads.
The girl, Jaidynn Penberthy, suffered a broken jaw, multiple facial fractures, broken teeth and burns, according to a GoFundMe.
Ethan Glass, Penberthy's brother, told local CBS affiliate KPHO that his sister was standing about 10 feet from the bonfire when someone threw a car shock absorber into the fire. It exploded, and pieces of shrapnel struck Jaidynn "square in the mouth" and rendered her unconscious, according to her brother.
"There was a lot of blood," Glass told the TV station. "It was like a scene out of a horror movie."
Partygoers performed lifesaving measures and Jaidynn's friends rushed her to get help.
She temporarily lost her pulse, and a friend performed a sternum rub.
"[Her friend] said that she lost her pulse for like a minute," Glass recalled.
Jaidynn remains at the hospital and expects a long recovery.
"At just 16 years old, Jaidynn is going through something no one should ever have to experience," the GoFundMe said. "The past few days have been incredibly difficult, and while there are still many unknowns, our main focus is making sure she receives the care and support she needs to make a full recovery."
Police said the suspect is in their teens or early 20s. Anyone with information is asked to call Phoenix police or Silent Witness at 480-WITNESS.
Glass told KPHO that he wants the person held accountable.
"Being kind of an older brother definitely makes me frustrated a lot. I mean, I really don't understand why he would do something of the sort. It makes no sense," Glass said.

title: Convicted murderer captured in Missouri a week after escaping Tennessee prison
text:
An escaped Tennessee prisoner convicted of murder was recaptured on Tuesday near Kansas City, Missouri, when his truck got stuck in the mud after troopers used roadside cameras and a helicopter to track him down, ending his more than a week on the run, authorities said.
Jacob Morley, who was sentenced to life in prison for killing a co-worker four years ago, was apprehended at around noon, officials said.
The Missouri state highway patrol says it learned on Tuesday morning that Morley was possibly traveling west on Interstate 70 in the Kansas City area. The vehicle was located using automated license plate readers and undercover officers traveling on a state highway in western Missouri.
Morley was driving a “metal flatbed work truck” with a white cab, said Sgt Justin Ewing, a spokesperson for the Missouri state highway patrol. It is unclear how Morley acquired the vehicle or where he was going. Morley may have had connections in the Kansas City area, but authorities don’t believe that he stopped at any residences, Ewing added.
A Kansas City police helicopter also followed the vehicle, which made it into Carroll county, a small county in north-west Missouri. Morley drove off the road and got stuck in mud, according to Ewing, and a Missouri state highway patrol trooper took him into custody without incident, ending a weeklong hunt. Morley was “compliant” when he was arrested, Ewing said.
Morley, 28, escaped from the Northwest Correctional Complex in Tennessee’s far north-western corner on 25 October, after he slipped through a fence in his prison clothes.
Surveillance video showed him stealing a truck from a farm near the prison, which he abandoned last week in Marion, Illinois, about 120 miles (193km) north of the prison.
Morley was serving a life sentence for killing co-worker Cody Birchfield in 2022. Birchfield’s body was found in a box under Morley’s home after he had been missing for a few weeks. The two lived in Carter county, in eastern Tennessee.

title: John Frieda, Celebrity Hairstylist and Beauty Entrepreneur, Dead at 75
text:
The world has lost a beauty pioneer.
John Frieda—a celebrity hairstylist who turned his expertise into a haircare empire—has died at the age of 75, a statement to his salon’s social media account confirmed on Nov. 3.
“John passed away peacefully…. surrounded by his family,” the statement noted. “John was more than a mentor to us; he was a true icon of the hair industry. He was the person who taught us everything, believed in us, and made us better.”
The John Frieda Salon added, “His talent and passion touched so many, and his legacy will live on in every single one of us. We will continue to do him proud.”
The statement concluded with well wishes for Frieda’s loved ones, affirming its founder will be in employees’ hearts forever.
Born Alan Howard Frieda in London in 1951, Frieda’s father Isidore Frieda—who owned a salon in Ealing—initially wanted him to become a doctor.
“I became a hairdresser for all the wrong reasons, to get out of studying," Frieda told The Standard in 2012. "My father was very angry. But when he realized I was determined, he said I must work for the top salon in London.”
It’s why, at the ripe age of 16, Frieda found himself working alongside acclaimed hairstylist Leonard of Mayfair, aiding on shoots with the likes of Twiggy, Jackie Kennedy Onassis and The Beatles.
One of the hairstylist’s earliest accomplishments was the development of The Purdey, a pageboy inspired cut Frieda crafted for The New Avengers star Joanna Lumley in 1976.
He opened up his own salon in central London that same year and, as they say, the rest is pretty much history.
Throughout his career, Frieda worked with clients such as Princess Diana, Madonna, Sarah Jessica Parker, Nicole Kidman, Scarlett Johansson and more.
In the late ‘80s and ‘90s, he pivoted from being predominantly behind the chair into hair care, developing his own brand of products. The most popular became his Frizz-Ease line, which is still beloved today.

title: Luigi Mangione's Cousin Narrowly Wins Local Election in Maryland
text:
Luigi Mangione's Cousin Narrowly Wins Local Election in Maryland
Luigi Mangione Killer's Cousin Narrowly Wins Local Election
Luigi Mangione's cousin has just won a local election in Baltimore last night by a very tight margin.
Nino Mangione -- a Republican -- narrowly won a seat on the Baltimore County Council, representing District 5.
Nino garnered 49% of the vote to his opponent, Democrat Shawn McIntosh's 45%.
Ironically enough ... one of the first topics on Nino's campaign website happens to be violent crime.
His campaign writes ... "Violent crime is increasing in Baltimore County. Every day we read or hear about another random act of violence against our citizens. Murders, shootings, carjackings, and robberies are all at record levels and are increasing every day."
Luigi's first cousin had previously served as a member of the Maryland House of Delegates from 2019-2026.
Up until last night's election ... Nino had served on the Baltimore council for 5 months ... after Republicans chose him to fill a vacant seat in June.
Nino's win comes just days after his cousin Luigi's legal team asked the New York state court to dismiss their case against him on the grounds of double jeopardy.
Luigi had previously pled guilty to the federal crimes of interstate stalking resulting in death and stalking through the use of interstate facilities resulting in death back in August ... in connection to the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson.

title: Woman Warns About Toxic Parenting Behaviors That Are Often Mistaken For Discipline And Concern

The first example involved an adult child making a decision their parents did not agree with and suddenly being labeled selfish or accused of hurting their parents. “Somehow, their discomfort becomes your responsibility. The second behavior, according to the creator, is when parents refuse to apologize but continually expect their children to accept that they are only human. “You’re told to forgive, to move on, to be the bigger person while they stay exactly the same.” The creator added that being a parent does not excuse a lack of accountability. She said these behaviors are not normal or healthy.
The TikToker said that if these patterns were part of someone's childhood, they may have had toxic parents. “Toxic parents don’t look scary. They look familiar.” She concluded by telling viewers who had experienced these behaviors that they were not alone or crazy.

title: Man, 57, Finally Completes Insane Walk He Started in 1998
text:
Man, 57, Finally Completes Insane Walk He Started in 1998
He was 29 years old when he first took off on his adventure.
A British adventurer has finally walked home after spending 28 years trekking 31,000 miles across four continents in an extraordinary bid to circle the globe. Karl Bushby, 57, was greeted by his emotional mother, Angela, and a cheering crowd outside her home in Hull on Monday—the same house he left as a 29-year-old former paratrooper in 1998. His journey took him through 30 countries, across frozen terrain and perilous jungles, and even involved 18 days in prison in Panama, as well as swimming across the Caspian Sea and the English Channel to avoid motorized transport. Bushby originally thought the challenge might take 12 years. Instead, visa battles, harsh weather and brushes with danger stretched it to nearly three decades. “They say it takes a village but literally it took a world to get me here,” he said, thanking the strangers who helped him along the way. He now plans to reunite with family, including meeting his son Adam, who saw him only a few times during his 28-year journey, and to meet his 12-year-old granddaughter for the first time.

title: N.C. man bludgeoned new girlfriend to death with a curtain rod
text:
N.C. man bludgeoned new girlfriend to death with a curtain rod
11/03/2026 9:47 pm PST
PITT COUNTY, N.C. (TCN) -- A 37-year-old man will spend the rest of his life in prison after being found guilty of first-degree murder for beating his girlfriend to death with a curtain rod in 2022.
According to a press release from the Pitt County District Attorney’s Office, friends and family members of 39-year-old Samantha Coppola called the police and requested a welfare check on Oct. 17, 2022, after they became concerned when they hadn’t heard from her for several days.
Her remains were found concealed in the home she shared with her boyfriend, Robert Edward Rathmann. Authorities believe Coppola had been dead for several days, and there was evidence of a cleanup at the scene. Law & Crime reports she had been bludgeoned to death with a curtain rod.
Rathmann was already in custody for an alleged burglary committed on Oct. 13, 2022, when he was charged with murder in connection with Coppola’s death, according to WCTI. Coppola’s family said she had recently begun dating Rathmann and they had not met him yet.
Rathmann and Coppola had moved to their new home in Grimesland, North Carolina, on Oct. 10, 2022, and Coppola’s family members heard from her for the last time two days later, WCTI reports.
The couple had previously lived with Rathmann’s aunt, who told them to move out due to aggressive behavior, according to the Daily Reflector. 
Coppola’s obituary reads, “A free spirit, Samantha was a devoted mother, had a good heart and was loved by all.”
On Oct. 30, Rathmann was convicted of one count of first-degree murder and sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole, per the DA.

title: Utah woman beat her shelter roommate to death with can of Ensure
text:
Utah woman beat her shelter roommate to death with can of Ensure
11/03/2026 9:43 pm PST
SALT LAKE CITY (TCN) -- A 62-year-old woman has been sentenced after pleading guilty with a mental condition to murder in connection with the fatal beating of another woman at a shelter in 2024.
KSL reports Laura Darlene Northrup killed one of her two roommates while she was staying at the Medically Vulnerable People Program Facility in Sandy, Utah. Stephanie Lynn Haskett-Carrasco, also 62, was found dead under her bed on May 26, 2024. She had suffered blunt force trauma to her face and neck. 
According to the Salt Lake Tribune, Northrup killed the victim by beating her with a metal can of Ensure nutrition powder, which was found with blood and hair on it in a bag under Northrup’s bed. 
The facility reportedly served veterans, seniors, and people with medical conditions who were experiencing homelessness, per KSL. Staff at the facility said Northrup and the victim argued frequently. 
According to KSL, Northrup pleaded guilty with a mental condition to murder on July 22. She received credit for time served and was sentenced to 15 years to life in prison on Oct. 29. As part of her plea deal, Northrup’s second-degree obstruction of justice charge was dismissed.
Haskett-Carrasco’s obituary describes her as a loving grandmother. “She loved to dance, sing, play, and joke with her grandchildren, creating memories that will be cherished forever. Her playful spirit and loving nature made her the best grandmother anyone could ask for. … Stephanie’s impact on her family, friends, and community will be felt for years to come. Her legacy of love, compassion, and joy will continue to inspire and uplift all who were fortunate enough to know her.”

title: Man arrested as girl, 17, found in Oregon after disappearing from Utah last year
text:
A 17-year-old girl who disappeared last year from Garden City, Utah, has been found in Oregon, and a 39-year-old man has been taken into custody.
The recovery of the teenager took place last Sunday, following a 500-plus day search involving Oregon law enforcement, the FBI’s Salt Lake City field office and the Rich county sheriff’s office in Utah.
According to the FBI, the man was taken into custody without incident.
In a statement following the girl’s recovery, the FBI director, Kash Patel, said: “Tonight, local police in Oregon brought a minor who had been missing for a year and a half to safety, acting on information provided by our FBI Salt Lake City field office.”
“We are grateful she can return home, and we will continue working with our partners to hold those responsible accountable. To anyone using gore groups to target and exploit children: the FBI and our partners are coming for you. We are using every tool at our disposal to combat nihilistic violent extremism, bring offenders to justice and protect America’s children,” Patel added, referring to online communities that target and extort children and teenagers.
According to the FBI, investigators with the agency and the Rich county sheriff’s office had been working on the case for more than a year, following leads from across the United States and internationally.
Authorities have not released additional details about the circumstances surrounding the teenager’s disappearance or recovery, citing the ongoing investigation.
However, local reports have identified the teenager as Kylie Arellano, who was last seen by her family on 29 May 2025.

title: Los Angeles Woman Charged for $18M COVID-19 Relief Fraud Scheme
text:
Related Content
Press Release
A federal grand jury in the Central District of California returned an indictment yesterday charging Marisela Nuno, 53, of Los Angeles, California, with an $18 million scheme to defraud the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) and the Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) program, federal stimulus programs authorized as part of the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security (CARES) Act.
According to court documents, the defendant allegedly obtained funds under the PPP and EIDL program by submitting false and fraudulent loan applications that collectively sought over $15.7 million in PPP funds and over $2.6 million in EIDL funds. The defendant is alleged to have submitted applications on behalf of businesses and entities she purportedly owned, knowing that the applications contained materially false statements and misrepresentations concerning, among other things, the purported entities’ number of employees, average monthly payroll, gross revenues, and eligibility for funding.
The defendant also is alleged to have submitted materially false supporting tax documentation with the applications. The defendant then allegedly used the loan funds for purposes not authorized by the PPP or the EIDL program, including for the purchase of private property, business startup costs, and payments to family members.
Nuno is charged with three counts of wire fraud and one count of money laundering. If convicted, she faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison on each count of wire fraud, and 10 years in prison on the count of money laundering.
